Graph of the Surface of a Smooth of Two Variables

Source: R/plot_smooth.R
plot_surface.Rd

Selects the graph of the effect of a smooth of two numeric variables (a tensor product modelterms7::te() or s(x1, x2)) as a raster with contour lines over the ranges of the two variables. With slices, the graph instead shows curves of the effect against the first variable at fixed values of the second, each with a pointwise band.

Usage

plot_surface(
  mask = TRUE,
  slices = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  vcov_type = bayesian_vcov(),
  n_grid = 60,
  legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

mask

Whether to mark the cells in which the interval of the effect contains zero.

slices

NULL, or a numeric vector of values of the second variable at which curves of the effect against the first variable are drawn.

level

The confidence level.

vcov_type

A vcov_method object, the variance of the effect.

n_grid

The number of points of the grid of each variable.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotSurface object, inheriting from term_plot.

Details

The effect is \(f(x_1, x_2) = X(x_1, x_2) b\), evaluated on a regular grid of n_grid points for each variable, with a standard error \(\sqrt{X V X'}\) from the block of vcov.StatmodFit() for the coefficients of the term. The raster is colored on a scale that is symmetric about zero. With mask = TRUE, a point is drawn over every cell in which \(|f| < z_{(1+\text{level})/2}\,\mathrm{se}\), that is, where the pointwise interval of the effect contains zero. The slices are the same function at the values slices of the second variable, and the bands are \(f \pm z\,\mathrm{se}\). A smooth with a by factor is drawn in one panel for each level.

See also

plot_effect(), plot_derivative()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x1 = runif(200), x2 = runif(200))
dd$y <- sin(2 * pi * dd$x1) * dd$x2 + rnorm(200, sd = 0.2)
fit <- statmod(y ~ te(x1, x2), distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "te(x1, x2)", plot_type = plot_surface(n_grid = 30),
                  data = dd)

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "te(x1, x2)",
                  plot_type = plot_surface(slices = c(0.2, 0.8)), data = dd)
